title: 4-A-Day RLA Daily Review
subject: rla
description: 8 Weeks of Spiraling STAAR RLA Practice for Grade 5

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The captain gripped the wheel as waves crashed over the bow. His crew looked to him for guidance, but even he wasn't sure they would make it through the storm. Still, he kept his voice steady and gave orders calmly.

What can the reader infer about the captain?
choices: A) He is inexperienced and unsure of himself.
B) He is a strong leader who stays calm under pressure.
C) He does not care about his crew.
D) He wants to turn the ship around.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a subordinating conjunction?
choices: A) Although it was late we decided to keep working.
B) Although it was late, we decided to keep working.
C) It was late, although we decided to keep working.
D) We decided although it was late to keep working.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The legislation was met with widespread opposition from citizens who felt it infringed on their rights.

What does the word infringed mean in this sentence?
choices: A) Protected
B) Violated or encroached upon
C) Supported
D) Ignored completely

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into food. Chlorophyll in the leaves absorbs light energy. The plant then uses this energy, along with carbon dioxide and water, to produce glucose and oxygen.

What is the main idea of this passage?
choices: A) Plants have green leaves.
B) Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make food from sunlight.
C) Oxygen is important for humans.
D) Carbon dioxide is a gas.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

Hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) Hyperbole
D) An idiom

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The team have been practicing since August, and their hard work has paid off.

Which is the correct revision?
choices: A) The team has been practicing since August, and their hard work has paid off.
B) The team have been practicing since August, and its hard work have paid off.
C) The team has been practicing since August, and they're hard work has paid off.
D) The team having been practicing since August and their hard work paid off.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Maya stared at the acceptance letter, reading it three times to make sure it was real. She had applied to the Young Writers Program on a whim, never expecting to be selected. Her hands shook as she called her mother.

How does Maya feel?
choices: A) Disappointed that she got in
B) Shocked and thrilled
C) Indifferent about the news
D) Angry at the program

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Renewable energy sources like solar and wind power do not produce greenhouse gases. Fossil fuels such as coal and oil release carbon dioxide when burned. While renewable energy is becoming cheaper, fossil fuels still provide most of the world's electricity.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Sequence
B) Problem and solution
C) Compare and contrast
D) Cause and effect

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The ambassador's diplomatic response helped avoid an international conflict.

What does the word diplomatic mean?
choices: A) Rude and aggressive
B) Tactful and skilled in dealing with sensitive matters
C) Confused and uncertain
D) Loud and forceful

questions.question: Which sentence uses a comma correctly with an introductory phrase?
choices: A) After the long hike, we rested by the river.
B) After, the long hike we rested by the river.
C) After the long hike we, rested by the river.
D) After the long, hike we rested by the river.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The two friends walked in silence, neither willing to be the first to apologize. They had argued over something trivial, but pride kept them from speaking. As they reached the corner where their paths split, one of them finally said, "I'm sorry."

What is the theme of this passage?
choices: A) Walking is good exercise.
B) It takes courage to swallow your pride and apologize.
C) Friends should never argue.
D) Silence is always uncomfortable.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

I was convinced that no one could run faster than me. Then the new kid showed up at tryouts and left me in the dust. I learned that day that there's always someone who can push you to be better.

From whose point of view is this passage told?
choices: A) Third person omniscient
B) Second person
C) First person
D) Third person limited

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The Underground Railroad was not an actual railroad. It was a secret network of routes and safe houses used by enslaved people to escape to freedom in the North. Brave conductors like Harriet Tubman risked their lives to guide people to safety.

Which detail best supports the idea that the Underground Railroad was dangerous?
choices: A) It was not an actual railroad.
B) It was a network of routes.
C) Brave conductors risked their lives to guide people.
D) Enslaved people wanted freedom.

rows: Secret network of routes and safe houses

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The scientists data showed significant results, however their conclusion was premature.

Which revision correctly punctuates this sentence?
choices: A) The scientists' data showed significant results; however, their conclusion was premature.
B) The scientist's data showed significant results however, their conclusion was premature.
C) The scientists data showed significant results, however, their conclusion was premature.
D) The scientists' data showed significant results however their conclusion was premature.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The mountain of homework on her desk seemed impossible to finish.

The phrase "mountain of homework" is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) Hyperbole
C) Personification
D) An idiom

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The archaeologist held her breath as she lifted the lid of the ancient chest. Inside lay a golden mask with jeweled eyes, untouched for three thousand years. This single discovery would rewrite what historians knew about the civilization.

Why is this discovery significant?
choices: A) The mask is made of gold.
B) It changes historical understanding of an ancient civilization.
C) The chest was hard to open.
D) Archaeologists like finding old things.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The candidate's rhetoric persuaded many voters to support the new policy.

What does the word rhetoric mean?
choices: A) Silence
B) The art of effective or persuasive speaking
C) Written instructions
D) Physical appearance

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct parallel structure?
choices: A) The coach told the players to stretch, to hydrate, and they should rest.
B) The coach told the players to stretch, to hydrate, and to rest.
C) The coach told the players to stretch, hydrating, and rest.
D) The coach told the players stretching, to hydrate, and resting.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Before the invention of the printing press, books had to be copied by hand. This meant very few books existed and most people could not read. After Gutenberg invented the printing press around 1440, books became widely available, and literacy rates soared.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Compare and contrast
B) Problem and solution
C) Cause and effect
D) Description

questions.question:
Look at the data table below about ecosystems.

Based on the table, which ecosystem has the highest average temperature?
choices: A) Tundra
B) Temperate Forest
C) Tropical Rainforest
D) Desert

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The general studied the map one last time. His troops were outnumbered three to one, but they held the high ground. He knew that if they could survive until nightfall, reinforcements would arrive. The decision he made in the next hour would determine the fate of the entire campaign.

What is the central conflict in this passage?
choices: A) The general cannot read the map.
B) The general must decide how to fight a battle against a larger force.
C) The reinforcements are lost.
D) The troops want to go home.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

Everyone in the class except Maria and I are going on the field trip.

Which is the correct revision?
choices: A) Everyone in the class except Maria and me is going on the field trip.
B) Everyone in the class except Maria and I is going on the field trip.
C) Everyone in the class except Maria and me are going on the field trip.
D) Everyone in the class except me and Maria are going on the field trip.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The sun smiled down on the children playing in the park.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) Personification
D) Hyperbole

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Screen time should be limited for all children under 12. Studies show that too much screen time hurts brain development, reduces physical activity, and disrupts sleep patterns. Parents need to set firm limits.

What is the author's point of view?
choices: A) Screen time is good for children.
B) Children should use screens as much as they want.
C) Screen time should be limited because it has negative effects.
D) Only parents should use screens.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The violin had belonged to her great-grandmother, then her grandmother, then her mother. Now it was Keiko's turn. The instrument was old and slightly worn, but when she drew the bow across the strings, the sound was rich and full of history.

What is the theme of this passage?
choices: A) Old instruments sound bad.
B) Heritage and family connections are passed down through generations.
C) Everyone should learn to play violin.
D) Music is better than sports.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The entrepreneur launched an innovative product that revolutionized the industry.

What does the word innovative mean?
choices: A) Outdated and old-fashioned
B) New, creative, and original
C) Expensive and overpriced
D) Broken and useless

questions.question:
A student wrote the following paragraph.

(1) The class organized a bake sale. (2) They wanted to raise money for new library books. (3) Each student baked something special. (4) The bake sale raised over $500.

Which transition word best connects sentence 3 to sentence 4?
choices: A) However,
B) In conclusion,
C) As a result,
D) On the other hand,

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution. These amendments protect important freedoms like speech, religion, and the press. They were added in 1791 because many Americans feared the new government might become too powerful.

Why were the amendments added?
choices: A) To make the Constitution longer
B) Because Americans feared the government might become too powerful
C) To create new laws about taxes
D) To replace the original Constitution

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The thunder roared like a hungry lion.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A metaphor
B) A simile
C) An idiom
D) Personification

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Plastic pollution in the ocean is a growing crisis. Millions of tons of plastic enter the ocean each year, harming marine life. To address this, scientists are developing biodegradable alternatives, and some countries have banned single-use plastics.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Sequence
B) Compare and contrast
C) Cause and effect
D) Problem and solution

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Liam had always been the fastest runner in his grade. But when Zara transferred to his school and beat him in the first race, he felt something he had never felt before — the motivation to work even harder. Instead of resenting Zara, he asked her to be his training partner.

What does Liam's response reveal about his character?
choices: A) He is a sore loser.
B) He is mature and uses competition to improve himself.
C) He does not care about running.
D) He is jealous of Zara.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a semicolon?
choices: A) The library was closed; so we went to the bookstore instead.
B) The library was closed; we went to the bookstore instead.
C) The library; was closed we went to the bookstore instead.
D) The library was; closed we went to the bookstore instead.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The journalist's unbiased reporting earned the trust of readers across the political spectrum.

What does the word unbiased mean?
choices: A) One-sided and unfair
B) Fair and not favoring one side
C) Incorrect and misleading
D) Boring and uninteresting

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The forest had always been a source of wonder for Mika. From her window, she watched the seasons change the leaves from green to gold to bare branches. She knew every bird call and could name each wildflower along the trail.

From whose point of view is this passage told?
choices: A) First person
B) Second person
C) Third person limited
D) Third person omniscient

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The boy in the wheelchair rolled up to the basketball court and watched the game. One of the players noticed him and tossed him the ball. He caught it, spun his chair around, and made a perfect shot from half-court. The entire court went silent, then erupted in cheers.

What is the effect of the boy's shot?
choices: A) Everyone leaves the court.
B) The players are angry.
C) Everyone is amazed and impressed.
D) The game is canceled.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The students' projects, which were displayed in the hallway were impressive.

Where should a comma be added?
choices: A) After students'
B) After hallway
C) After which
D) After were

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The Dust Bowl was a period of severe dust storms in the 1930s that devastated the Great Plains. Years of drought and poor farming practices had stripped the topsoil. Huge clouds of dust buried farms, forced families to migrate, and caused widespread economic hardship.

What is the main idea?
choices: A) Dust is a common problem.
B) The Dust Bowl was a devastating ecological and economic disaster caused by drought and poor farming.
C) Farms are found in the Great Plains.
D) People moved during the 1930s.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

She let the cat out of the bag when she accidentally told everyone about the surprise party.

The phrase "let the cat out of the bag" is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) An idiom meaning to reveal a secret
D) Hyperbole

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The mayor's controversial decision divided the community into opposing groups.

What does the word controversial mean?
choices: A) Universally agreed upon
B) Causing disagreement or debate
C) Completely ignored
D) Very popular

questions.question:
A student wants to improve this sentence.

The dog was big and brown and had spots and was very friendly.

Which revision is best?
choices: A) The dog was big, brown, spotted, and very friendly.
B) The big brown spotted friendly dog.
C) The large, brown, spotted dog greeted everyone with a wagging tail.
D) A big brown dog with spots was friendly.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Every morning before dawn, Mr. Okoro opens his bakery and begins mixing dough. By the time the first customers arrive, the shop is filled with the aroma of fresh bread. He has done this for thirty years without taking a single vacation.

What does this passage reveal about Mr. Okoro?
choices: A) He wishes he had a different career.
B) He is dedicated and hardworking.
C) He does not enjoy baking.
D) He plans to retire soon.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The invention of the telephone changed communication forever. Before the telephone, people relied on letters and telegrams, which could take days or weeks to arrive. After its invention, people could speak to one another instantly across great distances.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Problem and solution
B) Compare and contrast
C) Sequence
D) Description

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The prolific author published over fifty novels during her career.

What does the word prolific mean?
choices: A) Lazy and unproductive
B) Producing a large amount of work
C) Famous and wealthy
D) Writing very slowly

questions.question: Which sentence correctly punctuates dialogue?
choices: A) "I'll be there in five minutes" said Marcus.
B) "I'll be there in five minutes," said Marcus.
C) "I'll be there in five minutes", said Marcus.
D) I'll be there in five minutes, "said Marcus".

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The inventor had failed ninety-nine times. Each failure taught her something new about how the machine worked — and how it didn't. On the hundredth attempt, the gears turned smoothly, the lights flickered on, and the machine hummed to life.

What is the theme of this passage?
choices: A) Machines are complicated.
B) Persistence and learning from failure lead to success.
C) Inventors are always lucky.
D) It is important to give up when things get hard.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

Life is a journey, not a destination.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) Personification
D) Hyperbole

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The Hubble Space Telescope has been orbiting Earth since 1990. It has captured stunning images of distant galaxies, nebulae, and stars. These images have helped scientists estimate the age of the universe at about 13.8 billion years.

Which detail supports the importance of the Hubble Telescope?
choices: A) It was launched in 1990.
B) It orbits Earth.
C) Its images helped scientists estimate the age of the universe.
D) It is named Hubble.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
choices: A) While jogging through the park, Sarah spotted a deer.
B) Running down the street, the ice cream truck caught the children's attention.
C) After finishing dinner, we watched a movie.
D) Before leaving for school, Marcus packed his lunch.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

There are two sides to the debate about school uniforms. Supporters say uniforms reduce bullying and create a sense of belonging. Opponents argue that uniforms limit self-expression and can be costly for families.

What is the author's point of view?
choices: A) The author strongly supports school uniforms.
B) The author is against school uniforms.
C) The author presents both sides without showing a personal opinion.
D) The author thinks uniforms are too expensive.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The committee reached a consensus after hours of deliberation.

What does the word consensus mean?
choices: A) A strong disagreement
B) A general agreement among the group
C) A secret vote
D) A complete failure

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The small-town diner had been in Stella's family for three generations. When a chain restaurant opened across the street, business dropped dramatically. Stella could have given up, but instead she created new recipes and hosted community events. Within a year, the diner was more popular than ever.

What is the central message of this passage?
choices: A) Chain restaurants are always bad.
B) Adaptability and determination can help overcome challenges.
C) Small towns don't need restaurants.
D) Old recipes are always better.

questions.question:
Read the paragraph.

(1) The Amazon rainforest is called the lungs of the Earth. (2) It produces a significant amount of the world's oxygen. (3) My sister visited Brazil last year. (4) Deforestation threatens this vital ecosystem.

Which sentence does NOT belong in this paragraph?
choices: A) Sentence 1
B) Sentence 2
C) Sentence 3
D) Sentence 4

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The alarm clock screamed at me to wake up.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) Personification
D) An idiom

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Overfishing has depleted fish populations in many parts of the ocean. To solve this problem, governments have established marine protected areas where fishing is limited or banned. These protected zones allow fish populations to recover and help maintain healthy ocean ecosystems.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Compare and contrast
B) Problem and solution
C) Sequence
D) Description

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Nessa found a stray kitten shivering in the rain and brought it inside. Her mother said they couldn't keep it, but Nessa made a deal: she would do extra chores for a month. She kept her promise, and the kitten stayed.

What does this passage show about Nessa?
choices: A) She is irresponsible.
B) She is responsible and willing to work for what she wants.
C) She doesn't like animals.
D) She breaks her promises.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The diverse population of the city includes people from over 100 different countries.

What does the word diverse mean?
choices: A) All the same
B) Made up of many different types
C) Very small
D) Unfriendly

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct verb tense consistently?
choices: A) She walked to the store and buys some milk.
B) She walked to the store and bought some milk.
C) She walks to the store and bought some milk.
D) She was walking to the store and buys some milk.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The circulatory system moves blood throughout the body. The heart acts as a pump, pushing blood through arteries to deliver oxygen. Veins carry the blood back to the heart. This cycle repeats about 100,000 times every day.

What is the main idea?
choices: A) Veins are blue.
B) The circulatory system moves blood through the body using the heart as a pump.
C) Blood contains oxygen.
D) The heart beats fast during exercise.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The test was a breeze.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) Personification
D) An idiom

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The astronomer had spent twenty years searching for a signal from another planet. Colleagues laughed at her work. But one night, the radio telescope picked up a pattern that was clearly not natural. Her hands trembled as she recorded the data.

Why do the astronomer's hands tremble?
choices: A) She is cold from being outside.
B) She may have made a groundbreaking discovery.
C) She is upset about her colleagues.
D) She is tired from working all night.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The teacher asked the students to bring they're books to class.

Which is the correct revision?
choices: A) The teacher asked the students to bring there books to class.
B) The teacher asked the students to bring their books to class.
C) The teacher asked the students to bring they are books to class.
D) The teacher asked the students to bring theyre books to class.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The documentary showed both the beauty and the danger of living near an active volcano. Farmers loved the rich volcanic soil for growing crops, but they always lived with the risk of eruption.

What is the author's purpose?
choices: A) To persuade people to move near volcanoes
B) To entertain with a fictional volcano story
C) To inform readers about both the benefits and risks of living near volcanoes
D) To describe volcanic soil

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The obsolete technology was replaced by faster and more efficient devices.

What does the word obsolete mean?
choices: A) Brand new
B) No longer in use or outdated
C) Very expensive
D) Extremely popular

questions.question:
Read the passage.

First, the water in the ocean is heated by the sun and evaporates. Next, the warm, moist air rises and begins to cool. Then, the moisture condenses into clouds. Finally, the clouds release rain or snow as precipitation, and the cycle begins again.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Compare and contrast
B) Problem and solution
C) Cause and effect
D) Sequence

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The sculptor stepped back from her clay figure and stared at it critically. Something was wrong with the expression on the face. She had been working on this piece for weeks, trying to capture the emotion of hope. She picked up her tools and began again.

What does this passage reveal about the sculptor?
choices: A) She is satisfied with her work.
B) She is a perfectionist committed to her artistic vision.
C) She wants to finish quickly.
D) She does not enjoy sculpting.

questions.question: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
choices: A) The sun set, and the stars appeared.
B) Because the road was icy, school was canceled.
C) She likes dogs and cats.
D) He ran to the store.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The wind howled through the empty streets like a pack of wolves.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A metaphor
B) A simile
C) An idiom
D) Hyperbole

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The Great Barrier Reef off the coast of Australia is the largest coral reef system in the world. It stretches over 1,400 miles and can be seen from space. The reef supports more than 1,500 species of fish and 400 types of coral.

Which sentence is a supporting detail?
choices: A) Australia is a continent.
B) The reef supports more than 1,500 species of fish.
C) Oceans cover most of Earth.
D) Coral reefs are found in warm water.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The audacious plan to cross the desert on foot surprised everyone.

What does the word audacious mean?
choices: A) Boring and ordinary
B) Extremely bold and daring
C) Carefully planned
D) Canceled at the last minute

questions.question:
A student wrote the following sentence.

The museum, which had just opened last month was already attracting thousands of visitors.

What punctuation needs to be added?
choices: A) A comma after month
B) A period after month
C) A semicolon after month
D) A comma after attracting

questions.question:
Read the passage.

The cheetah crouched low in the grass, its muscles tensed. The gazelle grazed peacefully, unaware of the danger. In one explosive burst, the cheetah launched forward. The gazelle's ears perked up a second too late.

What is the most likely outcome?
choices: A) The gazelle escapes.
B) The cheetah catches the gazelle.
C) Both animals run away.
D) The cheetah gives up.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Schools that serve healthy lunches see students perform better on tests. Research shows that good nutrition improves focus and energy throughout the day. Every school should invest in better cafeteria food.

What is the author's purpose?
choices: A) To entertain readers
B) To describe different types of school food
C) To persuade schools to serve healthier lunches
D) To compare school food to restaurant food

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The old car coughed and sputtered before finally dying in the middle of the road.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) Hyperbole
C) Personification
D) An idiom

questions.question:
Read the two sentences.

The expedition reached the summit. The climbers planted their flag.

Which is the best way to combine these sentences?
choices: A) The expedition reached the summit, and the climbers planted their flag.
B) The expedition reached the summit the climbers planted their flag.
C) When the expedition reached the summit, the climbers planted their flag.
D) Both A and C are correct.

questions.question: A student is writing a research report about the water cycle. Which source would be MOST reliable?
choices: A) A classmate's essay about rain
B) A Wikipedia article about water
C) A published science textbook by an expert hydrologist
D) A cartoon about rain clouds

questions.question:
Read the passage.

When the town council announced plans to demolish the old oak tree in the park, twelve-year-old Amira organized a petition. She went door to door, gave a speech at the council meeting, and posted videos online. The council reversed their decision two weeks later.

What is the theme of this passage?
choices: A) Trees are very important.
B) One person's determination can create change.
C) Town councils always make wrong decisions.
D) Social media is the best way to solve problems.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The philanthropic organization funded scholarships for hundreds of underprivileged students.

What does the word philanthropic mean?
choices: A) Profit-driven
B) Charitable and seeking to help others
C) Government-operated
D) Small and local

questions.question: Which sentence uses an appositive phrase correctly?
choices: A) My teacher, Mrs. Rodriguez is very kind.
B) My teacher Mrs. Rodriguez, is very kind.
C) My teacher, Mrs. Rodriguez, is very kind.
D) My, teacher Mrs. Rodriguez is very kind.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Deforestation leads to loss of biodiversity because animals lose their habitats. This, in turn, affects the food chain, as species that depend on those animals for food also decline. The effects ripple outward, impacting entire ecosystems.

What text structure does the author use?
choices: A) Compare and contrast
B) Problem and solution
C) Cause and effect
D) Sequence

questions.question:
Read the passage.

In the time before time, Coyote stole fire from the fire spirits and gave it to the people. The fire spirits chased Coyote across the land, but he was too clever for them. To this day, people have fire because of Coyote's bravery.

What genre is this passage?
choices: A) Biography
B) Science fiction
C) Myth or legend
D) Realistic fiction

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Sofia noticed that her elderly neighbor, Mr. Kim, had not been outside in three days. She baked a batch of cookies and knocked on his door. When he answered, she could see he had been sick. She called her parents, who helped arrange for someone to check on him daily.

What does this passage reveal about Sofia?
choices: A) She is nosy about her neighbors.
B) She is observant, compassionate, and takes initiative.
C) She only wants to bake cookies.
D) She is afraid of Mr. Kim.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

The book, which I borrowed from the library, were fascinating.

Which is the correct revision?
choices: A) The book, which I borrowed from the library, was fascinating.
B) The book which I borrowed from the library were fascinating.
C) The book, which I borrowed from the library, are fascinating.
D) The book, I borrowed from the library, were fascinating.

questions.question:
Read the sentence.

I'm so tired I could sleep for a hundred years.

This sentence is an example of —
choices: A) A simile
B) A metaphor
C) Personification
D) Hyperbole

questions.question:
Read the passage.

We should all reduce our carbon footprint. Drive less, use energy-efficient appliances, and eat locally grown food. Small changes by millions of people can add up to a big difference for our planet.

What is the author's purpose?
choices: A) To entertain readers
B) To inform readers about carbon
C) To persuade readers to make environmentally friendly choices
